Messages.Author: Malcolm McCallum
Messages.Body:
My problem with the Duck and Dimple deck...

"What are we going to do tonight, Duck?"
"Same thing we do every night: Take over the Camarilla!"

...was apparently solved when someone mentioned that you can contest your
own vampires. So if I have a Duck in torpor, in my influence phase I can
bring out a new Duck (Contested), and immediately choose to burn the
other one? This sounds too sweet to be true. What's the hitch?

Messages.Author: R. Brian Smith
Messages.Body:


The hitch?
Well, while the rules don't specifically say you can contest your own
vampire, they also do not specifically say that cannot. There is only a
warning that if you do contest your own cards you will be subject to the
payment for keeping them. So you get people who attempt this type of
action.

Hopefully this will be clarified in future updates to the rules.

We (those who exist in the same gaming circle as I, minus one) consider
this another form of "weenieism" and find an effective counter with
"Vinnie" (Vinnie is the aluminum bat which I keep behind my door for late
night visitors)

but seriously folks

we find this kind of action to be very much against the spirit of the
rules, and have enacted a house rule that if you are stupid enopugh to
contest your own cards (or slimy enough to attempt such a degenerate
trick) then you give up both copies when you decide to stop contesting.
Sort of takes care of that problem rerally quick.

--

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <Pine.BSI.3.91.960530...@tubby.pacificcoast.net>,

Malcolm McCallum <mcca...@tubby.pacificcoast.net> wrote:
>My problem with the Duck and Dimple deck...
>
>"What are we going to do tonight, Duck?"
>"Same thing we do every night: Take over the Camarilla!"
>
>...was apparently solved when someone mentioned that you can contest your
>own vampires. So if I have a Duck in torpor, in my influence phase I can
>bring out a new Duck (Contested), and immediately choose to burn the
>other one? This sounds too sweet to be true. What's the hitch?
>

The hitch is that you can only yield of pay for a contest during
your untap. The second hitch is that you must pay a pool for the contest
if you wnat to end up with a Duck under your control.

So when you bring out a second copy of Duck, he will remain
contested until your next untap at wich point you can:

1. Yield both.
2. Yield one and pay one pool to contest the other (who will become controlled
if no one else has yet another copy of Duck in contest).
3. Pay two pool (one for each) to continue contesting both of them.

(Note that 3. isn't possible if one of the Ducks is in torpor - the torpored
one must yield during your untap).

Where do you see the degeneracy?

If you contest with yourself you are paying _quite_ a price:
- the action/influence to bring out the unique thing
- the blood/pool cost
- the one turns uselessness of the unique thing
- 1 pool to keep up the contestment of the one you want to control
- wasting deck/crypt space with multiple copies of uniques

I'm not sure if I see how this can lead to abuse...

Are you certain about that note to 3? I know that vampires must yield if

On another note, are you certain that contested cards return during your

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
Malcolm McCallum wrote:
>
> My problem with the Duck and Dimple deck...[CLIP]

>
> ...was apparently solved when someone mentioned that you can contest your
> own vampires. So if I have a Duck in torpor, in my influence phase I can
> bring out a new Duck (Contested), and immediately choose to burn the
> other one? This sounds too sweet to be true. What's the hitch?

The first "hitch" is that if you contest your own vampire during your
influence phase both vampires will be turned face down until your next
untap phase. The untap phase is where you must decide to pay a pool to
continue contesting or give up a contested vamp.

This probably won't hurt your deck much though. It is still easier to
bring out a new Duck than to try to rescue the torpored one.

See my Nosferatu Politics deck titled "Go, Duck, Go" in The Corrupter's
Deck Archive!

Sorry, at times I forget that the rest of the world doesn't share my
memories, funnny that.

It has to deal with a small vamp/fame combo.

Joe sixpack puts fame on a 3 capacity vampire. Joe manages to get the vamp
into torpor (not terribly difficult)

Joe then plays enchant Kindred or Govern the Unaligned to put blood
counters on a second, uncontrolled copy of the vamp in torpor.

During his influence phase, joe brings out the second copy of the vamp in
torpor. Contesting his first. At any time before his next turn, Joe gives
up the copy in torpor so he doesn't have to pay to contest.

Joe then plays Fame on the second copy that is now uncontested.

Joe finds a way to send that copy to torpor, repeat ad nauseum

All in all, Joe has paid MAYBE one pool, and has lost one minion's action
for one turn. That is not a big deal for that is what Joe's deck does. If
you know what Joe's deck does, it is easier to deal with. But sometimes
Joe's deck surprises you and you don't see what's coming until it has hit
you right in the nose.

and that is where I see the degeneracy. If I have overlooked some very
important point, please let me know.

This is just a guess, but I think that you are not allowed to burn a contested

flipped over until the untap phase of your next turn comes around.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <4p1sep$j...@gozer.inri.com>, Johnny Tullner <j...@inri.com> wrote:
>We thought you could contest with yourself for a long time, and believe
>me it led to many degenerate weanie decks.
>
>Luckily a few weeks ago someone finally found in the vtes rulebook that
>you *cannot* contest cards with yourself.
>
>

If you're referring to the passage in 15:
"You can't bring out more than one of the same unique card into your active
region.",

then you have a valid point, but not an official one.
This section is merely warning you that you won't have two of the smae vampires
in your active region - they'll both be out of play .

When you try to bring out the second copy, it doesn't go into
the active region - it goes out of play (along with the first coppy).

This is clarified in the "CORRECTIONS TO THE V:TES RULEBOOK"
<44dlot$1...@acorn.acorn.co.uk>:

Section 15, Contested Cards
Third paragraph should say "You can't bring out more than one of the
same unique card into your active region without contesting them."

Messages.Body:

>During his influence phase, joe brings out the second copy of the vamp in
>torpor. Contesting his first. At any time before his next turn, Joe gives
>up the copy in torpor so he doesn't have to pay to contest.

You can only "give up" (yield) a contested card during your untap, so
you will have to pay to contest the other copy (unless you yield both).
